name: Self-Directed Queries Complexity of Blockwise-Addressing
proof: Choose one block of $d$ $y$-coordinates. The $f_i$ realize every binary labeling on it, so an adversary can contradict all $d$ adaptive predictions on that subset while retaining a consistent target. Thus the subset-maximized self-directed value is at least $d$. There are $2^{d+1}$ concepts. On any coordinate subset, predict a majority label among the remaining concepts and use full feedback to restrict the version space. Every mistake at least halves its size, so at most $d+1$ mistakes occur. The source bound of two queries the selector and private coordinates on the whole domain; those coordinates need not be available in a prescribed subset.
references: \cite{ben1997online}, Example 2, for the class and whole-domain strategy; the subset distinction is explained in \cite{devulapalli2024selfdirected}, Section 2.1.
